enonce_markdown: A bank's clearing centre processes thousands of paper cheques every day. The account number and the cheque number are printed along the bottom edge in a special magnetic ink, and the machine can still read them even when a clerk has stamped over them. Which input method is being used?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Each automatic input method suits one kind of source document. Characters printed in magnetic ink and read by their magnetic signal are handled by MICR.

### Solution

The characters are printed in magnetic ink and are read from their magnetic pattern, so they stay readable even if they are over-stamped. This is **magnetic ink character recognition (MICR)**. OMR detects shaded marks in set positions, OCR recognises printed shapes by light and dark patterns (stamps would disturb it), and a magnetic stripe reader reads a stripe on a card, not characters on a cheque.

**Answer: d.**

A warehouse in Douala currently enters the details of every delivery by typing them at a keyboard. The manager proposes to tag each pallet with an RFID label instead.

(a) State **two** advantages of this automatic data capture over keying in the data.

(b) State **one** risk or limitation of relying on it.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Automatic data capture removes the human typing step. Compare speed, accuracy and cost against the dependence on equipment and tags.

### Solution

**(a)** Any two of:

- Data are captured **faster**: a reader can record a whole pallet (or several pallets) in a moment, with no typing.
- Data are **more accurate**: transcription errors such as swapped digits are avoided.
- The data go straight into the stock database, so stock levels are **up to date** and clerks' time is freed for other work.

**(b)** Any one of: tags and readers have an initial **cost**; a faulty reader or a damaged or missing tag stops the capture; metal or liquids can interfere with radio signals; a wrong code printed on the tag is faithfully copied into the system (the process does not check that the data are correct).

enonce_markdown: A digital camera produces an uncompressed image of 4000 pixels by 3000 pixels, with a colour depth of 24 bits per pixel. Take 1 MB = 1 000 000 bytes. What is the size of the image?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Uncompressed size = number of pixels x colour depth in bits, divided by 8 to convert bits to bytes.

### Solution

Pixels = 4000 x 3000 = 12 000 000. Bits = 12 000 000 x 24 = 288 000 000. Bytes = 288 000 000 / 8 = 36 000 000, that is **36 MB**. The value 12 MB comes from forgetting the colour depth (1 byte per pixel assumed) and 288 MB from forgetting to divide the bits by 8; 96 MB comes from dividing by 3 instead of multiplying.

**Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: A university library is replacing the bar-code labels on its books with RFID tags. Which statement about the two technologies is correct?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A bar-code is read optically, so the reader needs a clear line of sight to each label. An RFID tag answers a radio signal, so no line of sight is required and several tags can be answered together.

### Solution

RFID tags respond to radio waves, so a reader can read them through packaging and can read many tags in one pass, whereas a bar-code scanner normally needs to be aimed at one visible label at a time. The other statements are reversed or false: a bar-code is printed and cannot be rewritten, passive RFID tags need no battery, and a bar-code is not read by radio.

**Answer: a.**

choix.texte: An RFID reader can read several tags at once without line of sight, while a bar-code scanner reads one visible label at a time.
A bar-code can be rewritten many times, while an RFID tag keeps the data it was printed with.
A passive RFID tag needs its own battery to be read, while a bar-code does not.
A bar-code is read by radio waves, so it can be read through a closed box.

A school must collect the opinions of 600 students on the canteen. The head can choose between paper forms with shaded boxes read by an optical mark reader (OMR), or an online form that students fill in on school computers.

Compare the two methods by giving **two** points in favour of each.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Compare data-capture methods on speed, cost, accuracy and what each one needs before and after collection.

### Solution

**OMR forms**

- Very quick to process: a reader scans hundreds of sheets a minute, and the results go directly to the computer.
- Works without computers or internet access for the students, so everybody can take part.

**Online form**

- No printing and no scanner needed; the answers are stored as the student submits them, and validation (for example, a compulsory question) can stop empty or impossible answers.
- Results can be analysed immediately and the form can be changed easily.

(Weaknesses to note: OMR forms must be printed, shaded correctly and cannot capture free text; the online form needs enough working computers and connection time.)

enonce_markdown: A page is scanned at 200 dpi and the uncompressed bitmap occupies 6 MB. The same page is scanned again at 400 dpi with the same colour depth and the same page size. What is the approximate uncompressed size of the second scan?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Resolution in dpi counts pixels along each direction. Doubling the dpi doubles the pixels in width and in height, so the number of pixels is multiplied by 2 x 2.

### Solution

At 400 dpi the scan has twice as many pixels along the width and twice as many along the height: 2 x 2 = 4 times as many pixels. With the same colour depth the file is 4 x 6 MB = **24 MB**. Choosing 12 MB treats the resolution as if it only acted along one direction; 48 MB multiplies by 8; 6 MB ignores the change.

**Answer: c.**
